title: Quick check: Managing Sensitive Configuration

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Managing Sensitive Configuration”?
options: Public environment variables must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
questions.answer_key: Public environment variables must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Managing Sensitive Configuration: Public environment variables must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Public environment variables?
options: Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.
questions.answer_key: Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Managing Sensitive Configuration: Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Managing Sensitive Configuration” complete?
options: Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Managing Sensitive Configuration: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
